title: Europe seeks to deter Russia after attempted attack in Leipzig

Paris rents exceed legal limits at record levels
subhed: For the first time since rent control was introduced in 2019, 46% of properties in the French capital were listed above the legal caps, compared to 31% in 2025, according to the annual barometer from a leading housing group.

title: Writer Rebecca Solnit still has hope: 'When we show up, we can make the future'
subhed: Ahead of the midterm elections, Solnit calls for progressives to mobilize against Donald Trump in her latest book. She urges readers to reflect on the progress made over the past 70 years to understand the significance of feminist, social and environmental struggles.

title: France unveils €1 billion farm aid package after summer of drought and heatwaves
subhed: Agriculture Minister Annie Genevard announced a package of measures, including compensation for climate-related crop losses, tax relief for hard-hit farms and a new €235 million fund to help producers prepare next year's crop.

title: 'The question of meaning is the first you must ask yourself, even before taking out your camera': Jean-François Leroy, director of Visa pour l'image, pens letter to young photojournalists
subhed: In a book to be published in September, the co-founder and head of the international photojournalism festival in Perpignan, who died on August 31, addresses a letter to young photojournalists, urging them to approach their subjects with a journalistic rather than an aesthetic eye, and to learn from their elders.

title: Israel's right, threatened with possible electoral defeat, fractures and radicalizes
subhed: Ahead of the October 27 elections, tensions are beginning to surface within the governing coalition, particularly between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. From the right to the far right, political factions are hardening their rhetoric to rally supporters.
